entries.subject: ESO archive: raw table, calibration trees, headers and raw frames
entries.finding: The ESO archive serves VLTI raw frames anonymously: the raw table by TAP, calibration association trees by calselector, headers by its header service and frames by the data portal. A PIONIER frame took about 10 s on one connection, so nights download four at a time. The portal also answers 401 for minutes at a time to public frames (a Betelgeuse MATISSE exposure public since 2021 on 17 September 2026), so a 401 is retried before it is reported; frames still in their proprietary period are refused.

entries.subject: ESO data access policy for public archive data
entries.finding: Public ESO archive data are distributed under CC BY 4.0: a star cast from our own calibration credits ESO and the programme identifier of its frames, and derived files keep the ESO headers the pipelines copy into them.

entries.subject: ESO instrument pipelines for PIONIER, AMBER, GRAVITY and MATISSE
entries.finding: The ESO kits are public and pinned by sha256 in toolchains.json: PIONIER 4.0.4 (GPL-3.0, with Yorick, BSD), AMBER 4.4.5 (GPL-2.0), GRAVITY 1.11.0 and MATISSE 2.5.0 (GPL-2.0-or-later). They build on macOS with stated repairs: AMBER needs one package rebuilt for Apple clang 17, and MATISSE is rebuilt against LLVM OpenMP 20.1.8 because the kit compiles its loops out on macOS (759 s single-threaded, 479 s with 4 threads for one exposure).

entries.subject: PIONIER: π¹ Gruis September 2014 season from raw frames to a cast image
entries.finding: Two nights calibrated from raw with pndrs through image-star.mts match Paladini et al.'s file at a median squared-visibility ratio of 0.999 (828 pairs, no difference beyond 3 sigma) and give a reconstruction correlating 0.990 with the shipped image: cast. Lost fringes had to be removed before pndrs averages, and the author's 5e-6 squared-visibility error minimum applied.

entries.subject: AMBER: R Doradus December 2013 block calibrated from raw frames
entries.finding: One block against Ohnaka et al. (2019): median squared-visibility ratios 1.05, 0.98 and 1.15 per baseline and closure phases within 1.1 degrees, after per-baseline frame selection and CO-line wavelengths. R Dor's AMBER continuum does not pass the cast check (fit 1.74 and 2.99, spot ratio 1.31). The lost-fringe rule does not read AMBER products.

entries.subject: GRAVITY: calibration from raw frames and a season through image-star
entries.finding: R Car 27 January 2018 matches Rosales-Guzmán et al.'s file at a median ratio of 0.994 only with the authors' four HD 80404 calibrator exposures; the exposure the archive tree pairs gives 0.955. No GRAVITY season has run through image-star.mts.
entries.revisitWhen: A GRAVITY season (VX Sgr 2019 or Antares 2023) runs through image-star.mts to a verdict.

entries.subject: MATISSE: Betelgeuse February 2020 season from raw frames
entries.finding: One LM exposure matches Drevon et al.'s file on its high-visibility baseline (ratio 1.048) with differences up to 0.005 below V² 0.03. The five-block season (60 LM exposures) is pinned and the toolchain threaded, but the season has not run: about 7.5 min and 14 GB per exposure, overnight.
entries.revisitWhen: The Betelgeuse season runs from raw through image-star.mts and is compared with the authors' files and the shipped image.

entries.subject: What this archive holds for catalogued bodies
entries.finding: A name screen of all 498 catalogued bodies against the ESO archive on 2026-09-17 matched 144 of them, 145,077 rows across the whole archive rather than this telescope alone; the largest instruments are APEXHET (51456), APEXBOL (26625), VISIR (14125). Adaptive-optics imaging of main-belt asteroids with SPHERE and NAOS+CONICA is the part that could give unphotographed bodies a surface.
entries.revisitWhen: A candidate from the screen is taken up, or the screen is rerun per telescope.
